topline.text: Sheffield's finance and performance policy committee heard Monday that multi-academy trust chief executives have shown 'a real commitment' to reducing exclusions — but the council's own exclusions team is often only pulled in once a pupil has already been excluded, not before.
topline.action: Worth checking whether early-intervention contact is reaching MAPs schools ahead of a managed move or exclusion, not just after.

topline.text: A quieter day otherwise — nothing new broke overnight across DfE, Ofsted, SEND or national funding beyond what's already on your radar.

diary.text: NEU opens a formal strike ballot over teacher pay and school funding, covering 280,000+ teachers; closes 15 Dec, with action possible from early 2027 if it passes.
DfE response due to its EOTAS/alternative-provision SEND reform consultation, which closed 18 September.

items.lede: Council points to MAT engagement as the next step on rising exclusions.
items.body: Following Monday's committee report on the 32% rise in Sheffield exclusions, the council's strategic director for children's services said she had met multi-academy trust chief executives, who 'showed a real commitment' to keeping children in school. Cllr Douglas Johnson flagged that the council's exclusions team too often becomes involved only at the point of exclusion, rather than earlier when a placement is at risk.
items.action: Useful if you're approached about earlier support before a managed move or exclusion is finalised.

box.text: Teachers eligible to vote in the NEU's formal strike ballot over pay and school funding, opening 3 October and closing 15 December.
